original_question: What general structure results can be proved for smooth projective varieties with pseudo-effective anti-canonical divisor?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Proposition 5.3 (posed as an open problem despite the label "Proposition"): "What can we say for (smooth) projective varieties with pseudo-effective anti-canonical divisor?"
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main objects (smooth projective varieties), the positivity condition being weakened to pseudo-effectivity of the anti-canonical divisor, and that the paper is asking for a structural description rather than a single isolated invariant.
missing_details: The paper's nearest official target is not a proved theorem but the open-ended problem in Section 5, Proposition 5.3.
The ambient setting is complex algebraic geometry: smooth projective varieties over C, not arbitrary characteristic or general compact Kahler spaces.

In context, the intended benchmark is the nef anti-canonical structure theorem of Theorem 5.1, so "structure results" means an analogue of that theorem rather than any unrelated consequence of pseudo-effectivity.
The model conclusion in the nef case is phrased via a holomorphic maximal rationally connected fibration phi: X -> Y.
In that model theorem, the base Y is smooth projective with numerically trivial canonical divisor K_Y.

The model theorem also includes local triviality along the fibers, and even a product-type description after passing to universal covers; your draft does not specify whether these are the structure features sought.

The nearby discussion indicates that a first step toward this problem is to study surjective morphisms with pseudo-effective relative anti-canonical divisor -K_{X/Y}; this is part of the paper's intended scope around Proposition 5.3.
refined_question: Let X be a smooth projective variety over C with pseudo-effective anti-canonical divisor -K_X. What analogue of the nef anti-canonical structure theorem can be proved for such X? More specifically, does X admit a holomorphic maximal rationally connected fibration phi: X -> Y onto a smooth projective variety Y with numerically trivial canonical divisor K_Y, together with the kind of local triviality (and, in the nef case, universal-cover product structure) appearing in Theorem 5.1?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 5 rather than the holomorphic-sectional-curvature or pseudo-effective-tangent-bundle sections. The exact nearest formulation is Proposition 5.3 on p. 1025, which asks verbatim what can be said about (smooth) projective varieties with pseudo-effective anti-canonical divisor. That formulation is too terse to stand alone, so the correct sharpening is to import the surrounding Section 5 context: the immediately preceding Theorem 5.1 provides the model structure theorem in the nef case (holomorphic MRC fibration, smooth projective base with numerically trivial canonical divisor, and local/product triviality), while the paragraph around Problem 5.2 explains that a first step toward Proposition 5.3 is to study morphisms with pseudo-effective relative anti-canonical divisor. Section 4 is explicitly invoked as an analogy, since the nef tangent-bundle structure theorem has a partial pseudo-effective analogue there. Hence the most paper-faithful stand-alone rewrite is a pseudo-effective analogue of Theorem 5.1 for smooth projective varieties, not a broader classification question.
